verdict.rationale: The google/google-authenticator GitHub repository says the project includes one-time passcode generator implementations for several mobile platforms (HOTP/TOTP per RFC 4226/6238), so some client code is publicly inspectable. Nothing in the pack links that repository to the currently shipping apps, whose documented features (Google Account sync, Privacy Screen) are never tied to public source. Missing for 10: evidence that the current production iOS/Android apps are built from public source, an explicit open-source license, coverage of the cloud-sync code path that handles seeds, and evidence of community or independent security review.
